title: “Pathétique” finale: Furtwängler and the Musopen Symphony
work: Symphony No. 6 in B minor “Pathétique”, Op. 74 — IV. Finale: Adagio lamentoso
question: Furtwängler and the Musopen Symphony play the slow finale from its divided opening theme to the quiet low strings at the end.
intro: In February 1893 Tchaikovsky told his nephew Vladimir Davydov that his new symphony would end with “a most long-drawn-out Adagio”. The finale begins with a falling melody whose notes pass between the first and second violins. The recordings here are by Furtwängler with the Berlin Philharmonic and by the Musopen Symphony. Both play the movement through its loud climaxes to the quiet low strings at the end.

recordings.label: Wilhelm Furtwängler, Berlin Philharmonic
recordings.note: Furtwängler keeps the broad phrases of the lament moving and takes the climaxes in long spans.

recordings.label: Musopen Symphony
recordings.note: The modern recording contains the whole finale, from the opening exchanges between the violins to the final descent in the cellos and basses.

passages.label: Falling theme divided between violins
passages.note: First and second violins exchange notes of the falling tune. Neither section plays the complete melody; it is heard only from the two together.

passages.label: Second theme in D major
passages.note: Horns support a broad descending melody in the first violins and violas; trombones answer it.

passages.label: Descending scales to the climax
passages.note: Fast descending scales carry the broad melody to its climax. The whole orchestra plays the descent.

passages.label: Return of the opening theme
passages.note: The lament theme returns and builds to another climax. Trombones and tuba double the strings as the music moves towards a long-held F♯.

passages.label: Second theme in B minor
passages.note: The broad melody returns in B minor. Muted strings descend, and the tune sinks gradually towards the cellos and basses.
